stimuli.text: A block of mass 5 kg on a 37° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 8 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.15. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 0.4 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.1\cos(12t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) and a hoop (I = MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2.5 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A car moving at 13 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 6 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.
That is the stopping time in seconds.

questions.stem: Masses of 7 kg and 4 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the magnitude of their acceleration?

options.why: The masses are connected, so a is less than g.
The whole system accelerates: divide by both masses.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 40° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.

questions.stem: A 1.2 kg mass oscillates on a spring with $$k = 80$$ N/m. What is the period?
A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -100x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: ω is the square root of the coefficient.

questions.stem: A boat points straight across a river 200 m wide, moving at 8 m/s relative to the water. The current flows at 3 m/s. How long does the crossing take?

options.why: The perpendicular component alone sets the crossing time.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.
Correct. The current does not change the time to cross; it only carries the boat downstream.
The current is perpendicular to the heading.

questions.stem: A planet has 3 times Earth's mass and 4 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)
Two springs with constants 100 N/m and 20 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 3 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: The force is the weight, mg.
Series and parallel rules are reversed.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 4 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 17 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 0.5 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.

questions.stem: A particle's position is $$x(t) = 2t^3 + 4t^2 - 1t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its acceleration at $$t = 1$$ s?

options.why: The derivative of 2bt is 2b, which also remains.
That is the velocity; differentiate again.
Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.

questions.explanation: a(t) = 12t + 8, so at t = 1 the value is 20.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 200$$ N/m is compressed 0.22 m and launches a 0.7 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 53 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 16 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: That is in radians; convert to revolutions.
The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.

questions.stem: A 75 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 2 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: The acceleration changes the normal force.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
Check the direction of the acceleration.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.08\cos(2t)$$ m. What is its maximum acceleration?
A force $$F(x) = 4x^3$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 3$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 100 kg load 13 m at constant speed in 20 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 410$$ N/m is compressed 0.13 m and launches a 0.5 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.

questions.stem: A 2 kg cart moving at 7 m/s collides with and sticks to a 8 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 2·7/10 = 1.4 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 39.2 J.

questions.stem: A 1 kg ball hits a wall at 6 m/s and rebounds at 5 m/s. The contact lasts 0.05 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.

questions.stem: What is the rotational inertia of a uniform rod of mass 6 kg and length 2 m about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?

options.why: Correct. I = ML²/3 (parallel-axis theorem from ML²/12).
The mass is spread along the rod.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 6t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 3 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its position at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: Correct. Integrate twice, using the initial conditions.

questions.stem: A 5 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 2t^2$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 2$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Divide by the mass to get speed.
Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 9 rad/s and amplitude 0.13 m. What is its speed when it is 0.039 m from equilibrium?

options.why: Use A² − x² under a square root.
That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 1.7 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).

questions.stem: An object of mass 0.2 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.03$$ kg/s. What is its speed at $$t = m/b$$?

options.why: Terminal speed is reached only as t → ∞.
Correct. v = v_T(1 − e^(−t/τ)) and t = τ.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 65.3 m/s and τ = m/b = 6.67 s.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 1x^3 - 33x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Set the derivative, not U, to zero.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 3x² − 33 = 0 gives x = 3.32 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A 2.5 kg ball on a 0.4 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 6 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.
Correct. At the top, T + mg = mv²/r.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 5$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^2$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 16 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital period to A's?

options.why: Correct. T² ∝ r³, so T ∝ r^(3/2).

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$6 \times 10^{23}$$ kg and radius $$3 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: A 2500 kg car heading east at 17 m/s collides with a 1500 kg car heading north at 17 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Weight each velocity by its mass.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 20 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its time of flight?

options.why: That is the time to the top; the flight is twice as long.
Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 16 m/s, v₀y = 12 m/s. T = 2v₀y/g = 2.46 s.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 7 m down a 45° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.2. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 6 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 7 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 1 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 6 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.3. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Include friction on the table block.
Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.

questions.stem: A 2 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 1 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 7.84 m/s².

questions.stem: A constant torque of 2 N·m acts on a wheel ($$I = 1.3$$ kg·m²) initially at rest, through 4 revolutions. What is the wheel's final angular speed?

options.why: Correct. Work τΔθ (in radians) equals ½Iω².

questions.stem: A uniform 4 m beam weighing 100 N rests on supports at both ends. A 800 N load sits 3 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.

questions.stem: A 3 kg ball moving at +10 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 8 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 8 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -4.55 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 5.45 m/s.

questions.stem: A 17 g bullet moving at 410 m/s embeds in a 3.1 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Find the block's speed after the collision first.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.

questions.explanation: V = 2.24 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.255 m.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 5 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 1.5 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.1 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
